(i) a ~10 TeV G_ 1 can be discovered via Z + large missing energy signal at 5 sigma at a future 14 TeV pp collider with 3 /ab of data; (ii) a 5% mass determination of the lightest KK graviton is achievable at the same collider, based on the Z -> l+l- + missing energy signal.

the Z + missing energy channel can provide an efficient discovery mode for G_1 and a good mass measurement tool for the LHC and future hadron colliders, and that a future 100 /TeV pp collider can discover the singly produced G1 as heavy as ~10 TeVs.
the Z + missing energy signal can be an effective way of discovering the lightest KK graviton G_ 1 at the LHC and at a future pp collider.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the Z + missing energy channel, the discovery reach of a singly produced light G_1 at the 14 Tev LHC is ~2.5 TeV and the mass measurement is at the ~5 % level.
a light G_1 with mass ~2 TeV can be discovered at the 14 Tev LHC via the "Z + missing E_T" channel with ~300 /fb of data and the mass of the G_1 can then be measured at the ~5 % level.

a 14 TeV hadron collider with an integrated luminosity of 3 /ab would be capable of testing the Randall-Sundrum model of hierarchy and flavor with a ~10 TeV G_0 and a ~2.5 TeV G_2, which would be sufficient to test the validity of the Randall-Sundrim model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a light G_1, if kinematically allowed, can be discovered at hadron collers via the "Z + missing" signal, with the discovery reach being significantly higher than the reach via the "diphoton + missing" signal.
the Z + missing energy signal can provide a very promising probe of the warped graviton at the 14 Tev LHC and at future hadron colliders.
a light KK graviton, which has been long sought after in the Z(-->l+l-) Z (--> nu nu) channel, may be discovered at hadron collid- ers, if its mass is not much higher than 2 TeV.
